thread.previously: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed strikes on seven tankers in the Strait of Hormuz around October 23-24, 2026, one of the biggest single-day attacks of the war, unverified externally. Brent hit about $111-112 and was reported near $117 by October 27. Shipping through the strait is disrupted; Indian commercial LPG prices may change November 1.

stories.headline: Iran offers two-day Hormuz reopening as Trump threatens new strikes
stories.question: Is the Iran war about to escalate, or could Qatar's talks reopen Hormuz?
stories.dek: Both paths are open. Iran says Hormuz could reopen within two days if the US meets several conditions. Trump says one or two sites still need hitting. Oil fell on the hope.

so_far.text: The Iran war began in late February 2026. The Strait of Hormuz is the narrow sea passage that links the Gulf to the open ocean. Tankers leaving the Gulf must pass through it. By 30 October, Brent crude, the main global oil price, was up about 70% from a year earlier. On 1 November, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers struck mines in the strait. That claim has not been verified.

what_happened.text: On 31 October, Donald Trump said the US still had to hit "one or two sites" in Iran, which could be done "in 10 minutes". He named Pickaxe Mountain, a suspected underground nuclear complex. Iran denies any nuclear work there. Iran's Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, ordered that any threat be met with an "immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response". In parallel, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iranian negotiators were in Qatar discussing a plan to reopen Hormuz within two days, if the US lifts its port blockade and eases oil and gas sanctions. Qatar asked Iran to compress a seven-day plan into two. Washington has not publicly responded.

steps.text: Iran can slow tanker traffic through Hormuz with attacks and mines, which pushes up oil prices worldwide.
The US presses back with a blockade of Iranian ports and sanctions, which Iran wants lifted or eased.
Each side holds something the other wants, so Qatar's plan swaps them: US steps on day one, Hormuz reopened on day two.
But Iran's list goes beyond shipping: fewer US troops, an end to fighting in Lebanon, and released frozen funds.
If talks stall, Trump's threatened strike and Khamenei's order for an unrestricted response could widen the war quickly.

thread.previously: Americans vote November 3, 2026 in midterms deciding control of Congress. Trump pledged over $400 million to help Republicans and offered $1 million rewards for fraud tips; he has twice mused about elections not happening, which the White House called a joke. Over 18 million have voted early and polls are tight. The DOJ also sued over the Alaska Senate race (Sullivan vs Peltola).
thread.changed: A judge dismissed the Alaska certification lawsuit. Trump ended his 28-stop tour on 1 November. A Harvard forecast and an NBC poll now lean Democratic, and a Michigan Democrat endorsed the Republican.

stories.headline: Trump ends his campaign as forecasts lean towards Democrats
stories.question: What is at stake in the US midterms on 3 November, and which way are they leaning?
stories.dek: The vote decides who controls Congress. A Harvard forecast and an NBC poll lean Democratic. A Democratic win would let them challenge Trump's agenda and investigate his administration.

so_far.text: Midterms are US elections held halfway through a president's four-year term. On 3 November 2026, all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships are up for election. The House and the Senate together form Congress. The president's party usually loses seats in midterms. Trump has called voter fraud 'rampant', but evidence shows it is extremely rare. Even so, the Justice Department has opened probes or demanded that votes be set aside in several states.

what_happened.text: On 1 November 2026, Trump held his last two rallies, in Iowa and in Salina, Kansas. They ended a 28-stop campaign tour. "I'm closing the sucker down," he said. On 2 November the BBC reported that a judge had dismissed the Trump administration's lawsuit over Alaska. The suit wanted to delay certification, the official confirmation of results, if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan lost. It concerned two candidates named Dan Sullivan on the ballot. A Harvard forecasting tool gives Democrats a 96% chance of winning the House and 76% for the Senate.

steps.text: The president's party usually loses seats in midterms, so Republicans start the race on the back foot.
Prices are rising, which the BBC links to the Iran war, so Trump told voters Democrats would 'bankrupt your family'.
Trump spent his last days in Florida, Iowa and Kansas, states he won easily, which the BBC reads as defensive.
If Democrats win even one chamber, they can challenge Trump's agenda and run investigations into his administration.

thread.changed: New: on 31 October the INDIA bloc held a mock 'public impeachment' of Gyanesh Kumar. It passed a resolution seeking his removal and prosecution, which has no legal effect.

stories.headline: Opposition holds mock impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner over SIR
stories.question: Why is the opposition trying to impeach India's Chief Election Commissioner over SIR?
stories.dek: On 31 October the INDIA bloc held a symbolic 'public impeachment' of Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter-list deletions. It has no legal effect. Real removal needs a special majority in both Houses.

so_far.text: The Election Commission (EC) runs India's elections and keeps the voter lists. Its SIR exercise is a special revision of those lists. It is meant to add every eligible voter and remove ineligible names. Opposition parties say it wrongly deleted names. In March 2026, 193 opposition MPs signed notices seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. On 6 April 2026, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and the Rajya Sabha Chairman rejected them without giving a reason, according to The Wire. Around late April, 73 Rajya Sabha members filed a fresh notice. Thousands have protested in New Delhi demanding he resign.

what_happened.text: On 31 October 2026 the INDIA bloc held a symbolic 'public impeachment' of Gyanesh Kumar at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's Delhi residence. It had been put off from 30 October because of rain. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar led the proceedings, and Kharge moved the motion. The bloc listed six charges, including wrongful SIR deletions, altering Form 6 and sidelining the other two election commissioners. Its resolution seeks his removal, criminal proceedings including a sedition or treason prosecution, and withdrawal of his statutory protection. The resolution has no legal effect and does not remove him.

steps.text: The Constitution shields the CEC: under Article 324(5), he can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge.
A removal motion needs 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha signatures just to begin.
To pass, it needs two-thirds of members present and voting, plus a majority of total membership, in each House.
Opposition leaders admit they lack those numbers, and their March notices were rejected on 6 April 2026.
On 31 October the bloc held a symbolic mock trial instead. It listed six charges but has no legal effect.

After criticism over about 13 crore deletions, the EC ordered a special enrolment drive for voters who were left out. The mock impeachment itself changes nothing directly for you: it has no legal effect and does not remove anyone.

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu expected to hit south Andhra coast near Ongole overnight
stories.question: Where and when will Cyclone Murasu hit, and who needs to prepare?
stories.dek: India's weather office expects Murasu to hit land near Ongole overnight, 11:30 pm on 2 November to 4 am on 3 November. Chennai has had torrential rain; Andhra and south Odisha may get more.

so_far.text: A cyclone is a huge spinning storm that forms over warm sea. On 28 October, Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast with winds of 125–135 kmph. More than 1.8 lakh people were moved to safety. Odisha reported six deaths and 10 people missing. About a week later, a second storm is approaching. It is named Murasu, which means 'war drum'. India contributed the name. On 1 November, India Meteorological Department (IMD) chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra forecast winds of 80–90 kmph, with landfall on the morning of 3 November.

what_happened.text: By 2 November, the IMD's forecast had grown stronger. It now calls Murasu a Severe Cyclonic Storm. The IMD expects it to cross the south Andhra coast between Nellore and Narsapur, near Ongole. It expects the storm to hit land between 11:30 pm on 2 November and 4 am on 3 November. Winds at landfall are forecast at 100–110 kmph, with gusts up to 120 kmph. Torrential rain hit Chennai, Chengalpattu and Tiruvallur. Schools are shut in Chennai and in Andhra's NTR, Palnadu, Nellore and Gudur districts. Odisha has started moving people out of risky areas. Chennai airport said some flights were cancelled.

steps.text: A cyclone gets its energy from warm sea water, so it stays strong while it is over the Bay of Bengal.
Winds are strongest near the centre, so the coast near Ongole is forecast to face 100–110 kmph winds as the centre crosses.
Over land, the storm loses its warm-water fuel and weakens, but it still carries huge amounts of moisture inland.
That moisture falls as rain far from the coast, which is why Telangana districts are on alert and south Chhattisgarh expects very heavy rain.
The sea stays rough for a while after the storm passes, so fishermen are warned to stay ashore until the afternoon of 4 November.

analogy.text: Think of a cyclone as a giant sponge soaking up warm sea water. Over the sea it keeps refilling. At landfall the refilling stops, but the sponge keeps dripping as it moves inland. That is why districts far from Ongole can still get heavy rain.
analogy.breaks: A sponge only drips. A cyclone also brings strong winds and rough seas, which do much of the damage near the coast.

for_you.text: Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema may get very heavy rain on 2 and 3 November. South Odisha may get heavy rain on 3–4 November. Chennai and six Telangana districts are on orange alert. Check if your child's school is shut. Some Chennai flights were cancelled, so check yours. Fishing boats should stay ashore until the afternoon of 4 November. Bihar has a red alert for 2 November; its link to Murasu is unconfirmed.

misconception.fact: Rain keeps moving inland after landfall. South Odisha may get heavy rain on 3 and 4 November, and south Chhattisgarh expects very heavy rain on 3–4 November.

scenes.say: A second cyclone in about a week is heading for India's east coast. Where will Cyclone Murasu hit, and who needs to get ready?

India's weather office, the I M D, expects Murasu to cross the south Andhra coast near Ongole, between Nellore and Narsapur. The window is eleven thirty at night on the second of November, to four in the morning on the third.

The forecast got stronger. On the first of November, winds were expected at eighty to ninety kilometres per hour. Now it is a hundred to a hundred and ten, with gusts up to a hundred and twenty. Cyclone Arnab was stronger still.

The rain reaches far beyond Ongole. Chennai has had torrential rain. Six Telangana districts are on orange alert. South Odisha may get heavy rain on the third and fourth of November. South Chhattisgarh expects very heavy rain on those days.
Odisha has started moving people out of risky areas. It has placed more than three hundred rescue teams in advance. Schools are shut in parts of Andhra, in Chennai, and in Malkangiri.
This comes soon after another storm. Cyclone Arnab hit on the twenty-eighth of October. More than one point eight lakh people were moved to safety. Odisha reported six deaths.
scenes.show: Two cyclones, about a week apart

timeline.what: Cyclone Arnab crosses Andhra and Yanam coast
Chennai rain; schools shut; forecast upgraded

scenes.say: Remember this: the danger does not end at the coast. Rain may keep falling inland until the fourth of November. Fishermen are warned to stay out of the Bay of Bengal until that afternoon.
scenes.show: Rain may continue inland until 4 November

stories.headline: SEBI wants foreign investors freed from long-term capital gains tax
stories.question: Why does SEBI want to scrap long-term capital gains tax for foreign investors?
stories.dek: Foreign investors have sold a record $31 billion of Indian stocks in 2026 and have asked for tax reform. SEBI has backed scrapping one tax. The government decides, possibly in February's Budget.

so_far.text: SEBI, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, regulates the stock market. When a foreign investor sells Indian securities at a profit, India taxes that gain. Gains on holdings kept over a year face long-term capital gains tax at 12.5%. Gains on shorter holdings face a 20% short-term tax. In July 2024 the Budget raised the rate on listed shares from 10% to 12.5%. From 1 April 2025, foreign investors' gains on all securities faced 12.5%. In 2026, foreign investors have sold a record $31 billion (about ₹2.94 lakh crore) of Indian stocks. SEBI has met them several times over two years.

what_happened.text: On 2 November 2026, Reuters reported, citing sources, that SEBI has recommended the government scrap long-term capital gains tax for foreign investors. SEBI also proposed relief for Indian mutual fund investors. They would pay no long-term capital gains tax when they sell existing holdings to invest in new ones. The recommendations are advisory, and the government makes the final decision. SEBI submitted them ahead of the Union Budget due in February 2027. The reports do not say whether Indian investors in shares would get any cut.

steps.text: In general, an investor's real return is the profit left after tax, so any tax on gains reduces it.
When foreign investors sell Indian shares, they convert rupees into dollars, and heavy selling pushes the rupee down.
After a record $31 billion of selling in 2026, foreign investors asked SEBI for tax reform.
Scrapping the 12.5% long-term tax would raise their after-tax returns, which Jefferies says could support inflows.
The catch: JM Financial says lost revenue must be considered, and Bernstein's Venugopal Garre argues a cut alone won't sustain inflows.

items.name: SEBI
items.who: India's market regulator; made the recommendation

items.name: Government (finance ministry)
items.who: Makes the final decision on tax

items.name: Raamdeo Agrawal
items.who: Motilal Oswal; expects the move to be seen as positive

items.name: Venugopal Garre
items.who: Bernstein; doubts a tax cut alone brings lasting inflows

items.meaning: Record selling of Indian stocks by foreign investors in 2026 so far.
Current long-term tax on foreign investors' gains; listed shares were taxed at 10% before July 2024.
Tax on gains from shorter holdings; the reports mention only scrapping the long-term tax.

analogy.text: Think of India as a shopping mall that charges a fee when shoppers leave with their purchases. Other malls nearby compete for the same shoppers. Removing the exit fee makes this mall cheaper to visit, so some shoppers may come back.
analogy.breaks: Shoppers also pick malls for the shops inside. Investors also weigh growth, share prices and the rupee, not just tax.

items.view: Cutting capital gains taxes could make Indian markets more attractive to foreign investors and support inflows.
The move would likely be viewed as positive and could form part of the Budget, about two months away.
A tax cut alone would not trigger sustained foreign inflows, according to a Business Standard summary.
The revenue the government would lose must be considered, according to a Business Standard summary.

for_you.text: Nothing changes for your taxes yet; these are only recommendations. If you invest in mutual funds, one proposal could let you sell existing holdings and invest in new ones without paying long-term capital gains tax. The reports do not say whether Indian share investors would get any cut. The government's decision may come in the February 2027 Budget.

misconception.myth: SEBI has scrapped capital gains tax for foreign investors.
misconception.fact: SEBI's recommendations are only advice. The government decides on tax, and any change would come through the Union Budget due in February 2027.

next.text: The government will weigh SEBI's ideas while it prepares the Union Budget, due in February 2027. Watch whether the finance ministry accepts them, what revenue it would give up, and whether foreign selling continues.

dates.what: Union Budget due in February 2027 (exact day not given); possible decision on SEBI's proposals

Whether Indian share investors would get any long-term gains tax cut
How much tax revenue the government would lose
Whether the government has moved from its July 2026 stance of no plan to scrap the tax on equities

A foreign fund or investor buying Indian shares or bonds, not running businesses.
The government's yearly plan for taxes and spending, presented to Parliament.
A suggestion the decision-maker can accept or reject.

check.q: Why might scrapping the tax not bring foreign money back for long?
options: Investors weigh more than tax, and Bernstein's Garre argues a cut alone won't sustain inflows
SEBI has no power over foreign investors at all
Foreign investors already pay no capital gains tax in India
check.why: Foreign investors currently pay 12.5% long-term tax, and tax is only one factor. Garre argues a cut alone won't bring lasting inflows.

scenes.show: Why drop a tax for foreign investors?

scenes.say: That selling is worth about two point nine four lakh crore rupees. When foreigners sell, they swap rupees for dollars. That has put pressure on the rupee.

On the second of November, Reuters reported that SEBI, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, has recommended scrapping that long-term tax for foreign investors. It also proposed relief for mutual fund investors who switch funds.
scenes.show: SEBI recommends scrapping the long-term tax

timeline.what: Budget raises tax on listed shares from 10% to 12.5%
12.5% applies to all foreign investors' securities
Reuters: SEBI backs scrapping the tax

scenes.say: Opinions differ. Jefferies says a tax cut could draw foreign money back. Raamdeo Agrawal of Motilal Oswal sees it as likely positive. Bernstein's Venugopal Garre reportedly says a cut alone won't bring lasting inflows.
But SEBI only advises. The government decides. In July 2026, it reportedly told Parliament it had no plan to scrap this tax on equities. JM Financial notes the lost revenue.
Remember: nothing has changed for anyone yet. Watch the Union Budget, due in February 2027, for the government's answer.

sections.title: World
sections.gist: Ukraine's Oleshky truce ends as the US weighs Indian and Turkish Black Sea plans. Israel stays deadlocked, France protests continue, and the FBI blames North Korea for the Binance theft.

items.headline: Ukraine evacuates Kherson areas as local Oleshky truce ends
items.text: A short local ceasefire around Oleshky, in Ukraine's Kherson region, has ended. Reuters reported on 1 November that Ukraine is now moving civilians out of parts of the region. On 31 October, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US is reviewing Turkish and Indian proposals for a limited ceasefire in the Black Sea. He said international interest in the idea is growing. Separately, on 2 November Reuters carried a Wall Street Journal exclusive. It says the US is pushing to restart Russian gas sales to Europe through Ukraine. It is not yet known whether the US will take up either proposal, or when.
items.background: Russia and Ukraine remain at war. A US envoy met Putin on 21 October, but no wider ceasefire followed.
items.why: India's proposal is one of two the US says it is reviewing for a limited ceasefire in the Black Sea.

items.headline: Israeli officials say election results stand; Netanyahu calls vote 'stolen'
items.text: Israeli officials say the results of the 27 October election stand, Al Jazeera reported on 2 November. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claims the election was "stolen". Neither Netanyahu's right-wing bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's bloc won the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset, Israel's parliament. Netanyahu's bloc has about 53 to 56 seats, so it is 5 to 8 seats short. His Likud party has alleged fraud by Arab parties but has offered no evidence. President Isaac Herzog is consulting party leaders before he picks someone to try to form a government. It is not yet known whom he will choose.
items.background: This was Israel's first election since the Gaza war. In Israel, the president asks the leader most likely to win a majority to form a government.
items.why: Israel's next government will shape Gaza and wider West Asia policy. There is no direct effect on India yet.

items.headline: Over 300,000 march across France; masked rioters clash with police
items.text: More than 300,000 people marched across France on 31 October, some wearing Halloween costumes. The Guardian reported the protests were largely peaceful. Then police clashed with masked rioters, and the day ended in violence. The protests are against rising living costs, school funding cuts and budget cuts by President Emmanuel Macron's government. This turnout was smaller than an earlier rally of over 400,000 people. Unions have called a general strike for 5 November. A general strike means workers in many sectors stop work on the same day.
items.background: Protests over living costs and budget cuts began in September 2026. On 17 October, hundreds of thousands marched and about 1,000 officers were injured.
items.why: France is a major European economy. Long strikes can disrupt travel and business there. There is no direct effect on India.

items.headline: FBI blames North Korea for $6.3bn Binance crypto theft
items.text: The FBI says a North Korean hacking group it calls TraderTraitor stole $6.3bn from Binance on 29 October. That is roughly four times the about $1.5bn the same group was blamed for taking from the exchange Bybit in 2025. The FBI says the hackers are converting the stolen coins to Ethereum and preparing to launder them further. Laundering means moving money through many steps to hide where it came from. The FBI asked crypto firms to block the wallet addresses it listed. Binance says it has already replaced about 90% of the stolen funds with company money. It says users will not bear the loss.
items.background: Binance is a cryptocurrency exchange, a platform where people buy, sell and store digital coins.
items.why: Binance says users will not lose money. The theft still shows that even large exchanges can be hacked at record scale.

sections.title: India
sections.gist: The Navy signs ₹53,866 crore of contracts for eight corvettes it designed itself, and ISRO's NVS-03 launch strengthens NavIC.

items.headline: Navy orders eight home-designed corvettes worth ₹53,866 crore
items.text: On 2 November 2026 the Defence Ministry signed contracts worth ₹53,866.50 crore for eight Next Generation Corvettes. A corvette is a small, fast warship. That works out to roughly ₹6,700 crore per ship. Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) will build five ships and Goa Shipyard Limited will build three. The ships will fight close to the coast, hunt submarines and enemy ships, defend the coastline and watch the seas. This is the first project where the Navy designed the ships itself and government-owned shipyards build them. The Cabinet Committee on Security cleared the project on 29 October. Republic reported that the first ship is expected by 2030.
items.background: The Cabinet Committee on Security is the group of senior ministers, led by the Prime Minister, that approves big defence purchases.
items.why: The money goes to Indian shipyards. The ships will strengthen coastal defence and anti-submarine patrols.

items.headline: ISRO launches NVS-03 to strengthen India's own navigation system
items.text: ISRO's GSLV-F18 rocket lifted off from Sriharikota at 11:51 pm on 30 October. ISRO said it placed the NVS-03 satellite in its intended orbit. This was the 20th flight of the GSLV rocket. NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next-generation series for NavIC, India's own satellite navigation system. ISRO's chief said two more navigation satellites will be launched to strengthen the NavIC network. Each added satellite helps keep enough signals available for accurate positioning. The ISRO chairman also said the first rocket launch from the new Kulasekharapatnam spaceport in Tamil Nadu will take place in 2027.
items.background: NavIC works like the American GPS. Satellites send timing signals, and devices use them to work out their location.
items.why: A working NavIC helps India avoid relying on foreign systems for positioning, for both everyday and defence uses.

sections.title: Your money & life
sections.gist: Delhi's air crosses AQI 300 as commute curbs begin; commercial LPG and jet fuel cost more; UPI hits 25 billion payments.

items.headline: Delhi air crosses AQI 300 as winter commute curbs begin
items.text: Delhi's air quality index (AQI), a 0–500 score of how polluted the air is, crossed 300 around 2 November. It is the first time this season, and more smog is expected in the coming days. Winter pollution rules took effect on 1 November. They include 50% work from home, a ban on older vehicles and strict commute curbs across Delhi-NCR. Cars and bikes registered outside Delhi that fall below BS-VI, India's latest emission standard, cannot enter Delhi. Most dust-raising outdoor construction is suspended until 31 January 2027.
items.background: Delhi's air worsens every winter, so the government applies stricter rules on vehicles, offices and construction as pollution rises.
items.why: If you drive an older car or bike in from Noida, Gurugram or Ghaziabad, you may be barred from Delhi.

items.headline: Commercial LPG up ₹10; jet fuel rises for fourth month
items.text: On 1 November oil companies raised the price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder by ₹10, to ₹2,820. That is a rise of well under 1%. Aviation turbine fuel (ATF), the fuel jets burn, rose ₹1.37 a litre to ₹138.5. It is the fourth straight monthly rise for ATF. Restaurants and hotels cook with commercial cylinders, and fuel is a major cost for airlines. It is not yet known whether either will pass the increase on to customers.
items.background: Commercial LPG is the larger cylinder used by businesses; home cooking gas is priced separately. Both, and ATF, are revised monthly.
items.why: Small fuel increases for restaurants and airlines can feed into food bills and air fares over time.

items.headline: UPI crosses 25 billion payments in a month for the first time
items.text: UPI, India's instant phone-to-phone payment system, handled more than 25 billion transactions in October. That is a first. Their total value was ₹31.53 lakh crore. Put simply, that is about 80 crore payments a day, averaging roughly ₹1,260 each. The average daily value also crossed ₹1 lakh crore (₹1 trillion) for the first time. Siliconindia linked the jump to festive spending.
items.background: UPI lets you pay anyone instantly from a bank account using a phone app or QR code.
items.why: UPI now moves over ₹1 lakh crore a day on average, making it central to how India spends money.

sections.title: Markets & money
sections.gist: India's GST and factory data stay strong; Wall Street hedges against an AI slump; Britain set to hike, France's outlook cut.

items.headline: October GST collections jump 22.9% to ₹2.31 lakh crore
items.text: Gross GST collections rose 22.9% from a year earlier to ₹2.31 lakh crore in October 2026. That growth rate implies about ₹1.88 lakh crore in October 2025. Net revenue, which is collections after refunds, rose 25.6%. But the strong total hides uneven buying. Mint reports that consumer demand is holding up across categories. It also shows stress in pockets because of inflation linked to the West Asia war. That fits with retail inflation of 5.54% in September and the RBI's rate hike in October.
items.background: GST is the tax added to most goods and services, so collections rise when people and businesses spend more.
items.why: Strong tax revenue helps government finances, but rising prices are squeezing some households even in the festive season.

items.headline: India's factory growth eases slightly in October, PMI at 54.7
items.text: The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI fell to 54.7 in October from 55.1 in September. The PMI, or Purchasing Managers' Index, is a monthly survey of factory managers. A reading above 50 means activity is growing, and below 50 means it is shrinking. So factories are still expanding, just a little more slowly. Output and new orders both grew at a softer pace. The index remains above its long-run average and well above the 50 mark.
items.background: The PMI is an early monthly signal of factory health, released before official production data.
items.why: Factory growth supports jobs and incomes; a small slowdown is worth watching but is not a contraction.

items.headline: Nasdaq ends October down 5.3% as AI investors buy protection
items.text: The Nasdaq, the US index heavy with tech stocks, fell 5.3% in October. Most of the damage came at the end. It fell 1.4% on 29 October and nearly 3% on 30 October. Alphabet, Google's parent, dropped about 12% after missing earnings forecasts. Intel fell more than 28% on a weak outlook. On 1 November the Wall Street Journal reported that AI investors are rushing to hedge, meaning they are buying protection in case tech stocks fall further. The WSJ also reported that lenders now demand tougher terms to fund data centres, the buildings that house AI computers. It is not yet known whether the selling will continue in November.
items.background: Big US tech firms are spending record sums on AI. Investors are now asking whether those bets will pay off.
items.why: Doubts about AI spending are moving global tech stocks and lending terms. The sources report no direct effect on India.

items.headline: Bank of England expected to raise interest rates to 4%
items.text: The Bank of England is set to raise its interest rate to 4% to bring down inflation, the Financial Times reported on 2 November. Raising rates makes borrowing more expensive. That cools spending, which over time eases price rises. Other reports say the Bank may also push back on market bets for further increases. In other words, it may signal that this hike need not be the start of a long series. The decision date was not given in the reports.
items.background: The Bank of England is Britain's central bank; like the RBI, it sets interest rates to control inflation.
items.why: No direct effect for most readers in India; it shows central banks, like the RBI in October, are still fighting inflation.

sections.title: Tech & AI
sections.gist: Anthropic's IPO filing shows soaring revenue and big paper losses; OpenAI trims fundraising; AI firms back a training opt-out.

items.headline: OpenAI cuts its fundraising target to $20 billion from $30 billion
items.text: OpenAI has lowered the target for its new funding round to $20bn from $30bn, the Financial Times reported, as covered by TechCrunch on 31 October. The first close, the first batch of money actually collected, is expected to be lower still. The Wall Street Journal reported that OpenAI has secured $11bn so far. That is just over half the new target. Some large investors have responded without enthusiasm, the WSJ said. Fortune also reported a credit warning for Meta over its cash flow and spending.
items.background: AI companies need enormous sums to build data centres, and they raise much of it from investors.
items.why: Slower fundraising suggests investors are growing cautious about AI spending, which could slow the boom.

items.headline: Big AI firms agree on one signal for 'don't train on this'
items.text: Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic say they will honour a new instruction in robots.txt, a small file websites use to tell automated crawlers what they may read. The instruction, `__usage_ai-training`, lets publishers say they do not want their content used to train AI. Anthropic's Kevin Kelley wrote the draft. The rollout is staggered: Microsoft starts on 1 February 2027, Google aims for 2027, and OpenAI aims for the coming months. The proposal was submitted by an individual to the IETF, the body that sets internet standards. The IETF has not endorsed it.
items.background: Until now, website owners had no single, shared way to tell all AI companies not to train on their content.
items.why: Indian publishers, bloggers and creators could get one simple switch to keep their work out of AI training.

items.headline: Hackers target coders with fake AI tool and AI-powered stealer
items.text: Cursor, a popular AI coding app, confirmed that a Claude Code-branded extension in its marketplace was compromised. An extension is an add-on that adds features to the app. Microsoft published an analysis showing the extension set up a persistent SSH backdoor. That is a hidden, lasting way for attackers to log in to a developer's computer remotely. Separately, Cisco Talos described VOLTA, an infostealer, which is malware that steals data like passwords. In one stage, it uses a large language model to rank victims by how valuable their stolen data is.
items.background: Developers increasingly install AI coding add-ons, which run with wide access to their computers and code.
items.why: India has a vast developer workforce; if you use Cursor or similar tools, check which extensions you have installed.

sections.title: Science, health & climate
sections.gist: Ebola deaths in Congo pass 5,000, a very strong El Niño looks almost certain, and a second US dairy-linked bird flu case is reported.

items.headline: Ebola deaths in Congo pass 5,000, with no approved vaccine
items.text: Ebola has now killed more than 5,000 people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The DRC health ministry counted 5,340 deaths and 10,351 confirmed cases as of 29 October. That is about one death for every two confirmed cases. The outbreak was declared in May and has reached eight of the country's 26 provinces. It is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus. No vaccine or treatment has been approved for this strain. It is not yet known when the outbreak will peak.
items.background: Ebola is a deadly virus spread through body fluids. The DRC declared this Bundibugyo-strain outbreak in May 2026.
items.why: Over 5,000 people have died and no approved vaccine or treatment exists. The sources report no direct effect on India.

items.headline: Very strong El Niño likely by January, Ghana's weather agency warns
items.text: On 30 October Ghana's Meteorological Agency (GMet) said a very strong El Niño is forming and still getting stronger. GMet cited the US Climate Prediction Center, which puts the chance of very strong intensity between November and January at about 96%. That is close to certain. GMet says the El Niño will very likely last into early 2027. It expects a hotter, drier dry season in Ghana, with heat stress peaking from February to April 2027. It is not yet known whether the El Niño will last into India's June–September 2027 monsoon.
items.background: El Niño is when Pacific Ocean surface waters near the equator turn unusually warm. That shift changes rain and heat patterns in many countries.
items.why: El Niño years have often brought weaker monsoon rains to India. Weaker rains can hurt crops, food prices and water supply.

items.headline: Second person in Washington's Yakima County catches bird flu from dairy cattle
items.text: A second person in Yakima County, in the US state of Washington, has caught H5N1 bird flu after contact with dairy cattle. Reports on 1 November said the patient is in hospital with severe illness and has other health conditions. As of 29 October, 33 dairy herds in the county had tested positive for the virus. Officials say there is no evidence that it is spreading from person to person. They are tracing and monitoring people who were in close contact with the patient.
items.background: H5N1 is a bird flu virus that has spread to dairy cows in the US. Most human cases come from close contact with infected animals.
items.why: No direct effect on India. The thing to watch for is human-to-human spread, which officials say has not been seen.

sections.title: Formula 1
sections.gist: Antonelli, 20, becomes F1's youngest champion in Mexico, Hamilton calls for Ferrari talks, and Yamaha's Qatar exit raises Gulf race questions.

items.headline: Antonelli, 20, becomes F1's youngest world champion in Mexico
items.text: Italian driver Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1's youngest world champion on 1 November. He finished third at the Mexico City Grand Prix, which was enough to clinch the title. He is 20 years and 68 days old. Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race, ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton. The race had only one pitstop, on lap 28 of 71. Verstappen took control of the race there. The win lifted Verstappen to second in the championship standings, behind Antonelli.
items.background: The F1 drivers' title goes to whoever scores the most points across a season. Antonelli's lead became too big to catch.
items.why: F1 now has its youngest-ever world champion, and Verstappen has climbed to second in the standings.

items.headline: Hamilton calls for 'serious talks' at Ferrari after first-lap clash with Leclerc
items.text: Lewis Hamilton started the Mexico City Grand Prix on 1 November from pole position, the first place on the grid. At the start, George Russell, starting second, lost speed before Turn 1. That let Hamilton's Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc attack from third, and the two Ferraris clashed on the first lap. Hamilton finished second behind Max Verstappen. He said Ferrari must hold "serious talks" behind the scenes, and argues the clash cost the team the win. It is not yet known how Ferrari will respond.
items.background: Teammates race each other but score points for the same team. Teams usually set rules on how hard their drivers may fight each other.
items.why: Fights between teammates can cost a team wins and points. That makes Ferrari's internal rules a live question.

items.headline: Yamaha quits MotoGP's Qatar race over Middle East travel concerns
items.text: On 1 November Yamaha withdrew from MotoGP's upcoming Qatar Grand Prix. The company cited company-wide travel restrictions after assessing the crisis in the Middle East. Yamaha is the first manufacturer to speak publicly about the tensions around that race. Formula 1 still plans to race in Qatar from 27 to 29 November and to end its season in Abu Dhabi. F1 says neither travel advice nor insurance has changed since May. Imola in Italy is the reported backup venue.
items.background: MotoGP is the top motorcycle racing series. Both MotoGP and F1 hold late-season races in Gulf countries.
items.why: If teams start pulling out, F1's final two races, including the season finale, could move or be cancelled.

sections.title: Cricket — the masala
sections.gist: India take the T20I series 3-2 despite two late New Zealand wins; injured Chapman and Ravindra miss the ODIs.

items.headline: New Zealand win final T20I, but India take series 3-2
items.text: New Zealand beat India by seven wickets in the fifth and final T20 international in Hamilton on 1 November. India still won the five-match series 3-2. India had led 3-0 before New Zealand won the last two games. Adam Milne removed Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson in back-to-back overs in the powerplay, the first six overs when fielding limits apply. Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer then hit half-centuries. They added 93 runs off just 43 balls, more than two runs a ball. Tim Seifert and Glenn Phillips then guided New Zealand's chase. The two teams now move to an ODI series.
items.background: India and New Zealand played five T20 internationals. India won the first three to clinch the series early.
items.why: India won the series, but New Zealand won the last two games heading into the ODI series.

items.headline: Chapman and Ravindra injured, miss New Zealand's ODIs against India
items.text: Mark Chapman and Rachin Ravindra will miss New Zealand's one-day international (ODI) series against India. New Zealand Cricket said on 2 November that neither has recovered from injury. New Zealand has reshuffled its squad. Tim Seifert, who helped steer the win in the final T20I on 1 November, is now picked for the whole ODI series. Henry Nicholls joins for the first three ODIs. Foxcroft comes in for the last two. The match dates were not given in the sources.
items.background: After the T20 series, which India won 3-2, India and New Zealand play an ODI series, with 50 overs per side.
items.why: New Zealand will face India without two squad players, and the ODI squad changes partway through the series.

also.text: North Korea tested a cluster-bomb warhead for tactical ballistic missiles on Oct 31, vowing four warhead types by end-2026.
Taiwan accused China of harassment after a standoff between coast guard ships.
Tusk vows to press on with overhaul of Poland's Constitutional Tribunal; the president calls it a forced takeover.
France's National Assembly backed a 2027 budget amendment charging content providers €0.055 per gigabyte delivered in France.
AAP names 40 sitting MLAs for 2027 Punjab polls; CM Bhagwant Mann to contest from Dhuri.
Six people died in an Oct. 30 helicopter crash near Joshimath, Uttarakhand; remains were flown to AIIMS Rishikesh.
Jio says mobile tariff hikes can wait and it is seeking 10-15 partners for overseas expansion.
Digi Yatra begins international passenger trials at seven Indian airports, with wider rollout planned for 2027.
Coal India unit SECL files draft papers with SEBI for an IPO of up to 66.81 crore shares.
EU began charging a €2 handling fee per product category on small parcels from Shein, Temu and similar platforms on Nov. 1.
Namibia beat Ireland 3-2 for their first bilateral ODI series win.

quiz.q: Why did oil prices fall on 2 November even though no deal was signed?
options: Hormuz had already fully reopened to tankers
Traders hoped the Qatar talks could reopen Hormuz soon
The US had lifted its sanctions on Iran
quiz.why: Prices moved on hope. Qatar's two-day plan raised the chance of tankers moving freely again, but the US has not responded and nothing is agreed.

quiz.q: Why does the BBC see Trump's final rallies in Florida, Iowa and Kansas as telling?
options: They are the closest swing states in the country
He won them easily before, so defending them suggests Republicans are worried
They hold most of the House seats on the ballot
quiz.why: Campaigning in states you already won easily signals defence, not attack. The BBC says that shows how tight the race could be.

quiz.q: What would it actually take to remove the Chief Election Commissioner from office?
options: Two-thirds of members present and voting, plus a majority of total membership, in each House
